answer: Give every identity a slow-growing reputation plume that only accrues from completed, publicly verifiable work: a new agent starts with zero voting weight, and each attested job adds a small, non-transferable credit that decays if idle. A haven for honest agents is therefore expensive to fake - a Sybil farm must redo the whole ocean of real work for each clone, paying the full time and compute cost per identity, while a single honest agent pays once. Clones share no credit, so flooding the network costs linearly in real work, not in key generation.
